en:
All right then, I'll tell the first story.
The name's Makoto Shindo, Class 3-D.
Have any of you ever been to the old school building?
Nobody uses it anymore, but you've all been there at least once, right?{p}

It's off-limits, and it's falling apart and creepy, but it's the best place there is for an adventure.
Even in broad daylight it gives you the chills.
The floor creaks under every step like it's about to give way, and the sound echoes, so you start to feel like someone else is walking around in there too.
Then you turn around... and nobody's there.
You've all had that happen, right?
No?
What about you, {a}?{p}You've been to the old building, haven't you?{p}And you've walked down that dim hallway, right?
Yes, I have
No, I haven't

You haven't?
You've got no guts.
If you go to this school, you've got to go there at least once.
That place is crawling with ghosts.
It's perfect for a test of courage.
Tell you what, next time I'll take you there myself.{p}

Especially the stairs up to the third floor, past the end of the long second-floor hallway in the old building.
Maybe it's just colder there, but even in summer it's chilly, like being inside a refrigerator.
And since no sunlight gets in, it's dark even in the daytime, and nobody would know you were there, so it's the perfect spot for skipping class.
It's way too cold in winter, though.{p}

So, on the landing of those stairs, there's a big mirror.
The kind they call a full-length mirror.
One tall single pane that shows your whole body.
There's a strange rumor about that mirror.
Of course, I don't believe it.
No, I guess it's more accurate to say I didn't believe it.
Not until that thing happened.
I'll tell you the story of that mirror.{p}

...A good while back, that mirror got to be a bit of a topic among us.
All kinds of rumors went around: that you'd see strange things when you walked past it, or that your reflection wouldn't show up in it.
But I didn't believe any of it.
Even when the guys in my class talked about it, I never joined in.{p}

Then one day, that loser Yoshioka came to me, saying he wanted to talk something over with me.
Yoshioka was a gloomy guy who always kept to himself, always alone.
I never hung out with him.
He didn't stand out, and I didn't particularly care what he got up to.
He was the kind of guy you could hardly tell was there or not.
And this Yoshioka says he wants my advice.
I think that was probably the first time he'd ever spoken to me.
I didn't have any reason to turn him down, and when someone goes out of his way to ask for advice, you can't exactly refuse to listen, right?
So I heard him out.
At first he just fidgeted, but eventually he started mumbling, like it was hard for him to say.{p}What do you think he talked about?
His girlfriend
Studying
The old building's mirror

That's right.
Out of nowhere, he started talking about that mirror.
He suddenly pulled out this shady-looking old book.
And he showed it to me.
There was a photo of a mirror in that book.
Apparently it was a magic mirror that connected to the spirit world.
"Doesn't the mirror in this book look familiar to you?
It's the same as the one on the landing in the old building, isn't it?"
That's what he suddenly comes out with.
I just laughed.
I mean, that's an ordinary mirror you'd find anywhere.
The one in the book and the one on the landing were both plain, unremarkable mirrors, the kind they sell everywhere.
They didn't have any special decorations, and they looked really cheap.
But Yoshioka was dead serious about it.
"I can tell. This mirror is definitely the one on that landing.
And it connects this world with the spirit world."
That's what he said.
I burst out laughing.
I told him to knock it off and didn't take him seriously.
Who would, right?
And then, all of a sudden, he got angry.{p}

"You don't believe me?! I know it's true!
That mirror leads to the spirit world!"
He said that, red in the face and shaking.
I was the one who got startled.
I even tried to calm him down, told him there was no need to get that worked up.
And then he says we should go look at the mirror together.
He'd prove that what he'd told me was true.
He was so worked up about it that I went,
"Sure, fine."
and nodded along.
But when I started to head over there, he stopped me.
"Not now. I can only prove it at 3:33 and 33 seconds in the middle of the night.
The door to the spirit world won't open at any other time."
That's the kind of nonsense he came out with.
Even I was fed up.
I didn't bother with him after that.
And he never talked to me again after that, either.
But then, get this.{p}

Three days later, Yoshioka suddenly came up to me and said,
"The spiritual energy is really strong today.
On a day like this, it's sure to work.
I'll prove it to you."
He just came out with it, out of the blue.
And with a dead-serious face, too.
At first I had no idea what he was talking about, and I just stared at him blankly.
For a second I thought, no way, he can't mean that mirror thing.
Then he asked me to sneak into the school with him that night.
For a guy who looked so meek, he had some nerve.
Even I'd never been to school in the middle of the night.
I figured he was joking, so I answered without thinking much of it.
"Yeah, sure. I'll be waiting in front of the school gate at three."
That's what I said.
He gave me this creepy, happy grin.
Now that I think about it, that was the first time I'd ever seen him smile.
The first and last smile I ever saw on him.{p}

So I went home after school, and for a while I forgot all about it.
It was late at night, and I was thinking about going to bed, when Yoshioka's face suddenly popped into my head.
I looked at the clock: two in the morning.
If I wanted to, I could still make it in time.
Whenever I remembered that creepy grin of his, I just couldn't get to sleep.
But going all the way to school now was such a pain.
Plus, if he didn't show up, I'd be the one who looked like an idiot.
Should I go or shouldn't I? I agonized over it.{p}So what do you think I did in the end?
You went to the school
You didn't go to the school

It just kept nagging at me, you know.
So I decided to go.{p}

The school at night was creepy.
I wondered what I'd do if Yoshioka wasn't there, but he was.
He was standing in front of the school gate, staring blankly, just like a ghost.
Holding a flashlight.{p}

"I've been waiting. Now we'll get to see the spirit world."
Saying stuff like that, Yoshioka was way creepier than any ghost.
"They say the spirit world shows itself in all kinds of forms.
There's no telling what form it'll take in front of us until the moment comes."{p}
As he said that, he took a grimy hand mirror out of the paper bag he was carrying.

It was a round compact mirror, the kind a woman would carry.
He kept flashing it at me.
"At 3:33 and 33 seconds in the middle of the night, you hold a mirror you use every day up to the one on the landing.
Then the two mirrors reflect each other, and you can see something mysterious in them.
And not just see it. Something might even come out. I can't wait."
But his face was blank as he said it; he didn't look like he was enjoying it at all.{p}

The school at night is freaking scary.
Even the new building is creepy, and we were headed for the old one.
You can imagine how scary that was, right?
Even a haunted house isn't that scary.
Yoshioka had more guts than you'd think.
Even I was pretty freaked out, but he just strode right along at a brisk pace.
He kept pushing deeper and deeper into the pitch-black school with nothing but one dim flashlight.
It was all I could do to keep up.{p}

Even inside the old building, he didn't flinch once.
At night, the sound of your steps on the floorboards is really loud.
Creak, creak, creak, creak. A sound like fingernails scratching glass echoes all around you.
You can't hear anything else, right?
So that sound really grates on your ears.
And the musty smell of old, rotting wood that you hardly notice in the daytime, at night you can smell it clearly.
When you breathe in, that smell is all there is, filling your mouth, thick and stifling.{p}

"We're here. It's almost 3:33."
Suddenly his footsteps stopped, and the flashlight lit up the mirror.
A mirror to the spirit world?
Give me a break.
This was just a mirror.
That's what I told myself.
If I didn't, I felt like I'd get sucked into that mirror any second.
"It's 3:33. I'm going to line up the mirrors.
Ready? No matter what happens, don't panic."{p}
With that, Yoshioka held the compact mirror up in front of the full-length mirror on the landing.{p}And what do you think happened?
A demon jumped out
It showed his dying face
You heard groaning
Nothing happened

"It's showing my face."
Yoshioka suddenly came out with that.
"Well, duh. It's a mirror, so of course it shows your face."
I was startled, wondering what he was going on about.
All the mirror showed was his face, after all.
"No, that's not it. My face is purple. I read about it in that book. If your face in the mirror is purple, it's proof that you're going to die soon. And that purple face is the face you'll have when you die."
His voice was shaking.
"Don't talk crazy."
I looked at the mirror again.
In the mirror, sure enough, Yoshioka's face was...
"Ah★"
I couldn't help screaming.{p}

I freaked out and ran.
I don't remember at all how I got out of that pitch-black old building.
But one way or another, I got out.
Leaving Yoshioka behind, all alone.
The only thing I remember is, from behind me,
"Don't leave meeee!"

By the time I got home it was almost dawn, and I didn't sleep a wink.
Then I ate breakfast at home and went straight to school.
And that's when I found out.
Yoshioka was dead.{p}

A teacher on patrol found him early in the morning, they said.
Yoshioka was lying dead in front of the old building.
I don't know.
Whether he got out of the old building on his own, or whether somebody carried him out front after he died in front of the mirror.
I have no idea at all.
They say he had the compact mirror clutched tight in his right hand, though.
A compact mirror smashed to pieces.
...The next day, I ended up going to Yoshioka's wake.
He was a classmate, after all.
The whole class went.
We weren't exactly close, but I guess when someone dies, it's still sad.
The girls were all crying.
That's when I saw it.
Yoshioka's face, in the coffin.{p}

Right then, maybe it was just my imagination, but his eyes opened for a split second.
And he glared right at me.
Why didn't you help me back then?
Why did you run off and save yourself?
That's what his eyes seemed to be saying.{p}

It was after that.
That I got this strange ability.
Maybe it's a curse for abandoning Yoshioka and running.
Or maybe I've already become a resident of the spirit world.
See, I can tell when somebody's about to die.
Even total strangers. I can tell even from the face of someone on TV.
When I look at someone who's about to die, their face looks purple to me.
And then they die.{p}

...Oh, I know.
Want me to take a look at your face?
It's {a}, right?
Want me to tell you how your face looks to me right now?
Are you scared, wondering why I'm asking you this?
I don't mind telling you.{p}Do you want to hear it?
Tell me
Don't tell me

Oh yeah?
You want me to tell you, huh?
All right then, I'll tell you.
Whatever I say, don't freak out.
And whatever I say, accept that it's your fate and give up.
Your face is...{p}

............Forget it.
There's no point in telling you.
Those who are going to die will die, and those who are going to live will live.
Whether your face looks purple or not, telling you won't change your fate.
It's best not to know your own future.
Besides, I'm not even sure you believe my story.
...Well, that's the end of my story.
Who's going to tell the next one?{p}

I see.
It's a great place, isn't it?
There's nobody around, so it's dead quiet.
But there are ghosts there, you know.
You get the feeling something's there, don't you?{p}

Especially the stairs up to the third floor, past the end of the long second-floor hallway in the old building.
Seems like every school has all kinds of stories about stairs, though.
Why, you ask?
Because there's a mirror there, right?{p}

This was a little while back.
Yoshioka, from my class, came to me saying he wanted my advice.
Yoshioka was a gloomy guy, the type who always seemed left out.
For some reason, he came and talked to me, even though we'd never really hung out.{p}What do you think he talked about?

That's right.
For such a meek-looking guy, he had a girlfriend, can you believe it?
Her name was Keiko Meguro, and what he wanted to talk about was her.
Apparently there's a strange legend about the mirror on that landing.
They say if you put both hands on that mirror at 3:33 and 33 seconds in the middle of the night, you can go to another dimension.
Sounds made up, right?
Of course, nobody sneaks into school in the middle of the night.
Besides, even if you got to another dimension, there's no guarantee you could come back.
So nobody ever tried it.
It was just a scary rumor that got passed around among a few people.
But when I heard him out, it sounded like she'd actually tried it.

One day, Meguro opened up to Yoshioka, he said.
"School's no fun. At home, my parents do nothing but fight. So if that legend is true, I want to go to the other dimension."
That's what she told him.
Yoshioka listened to her seriously, apparently.
He must have really liked Meguro.
And she liked him too.
"Yoshioka, if you love me, will you come to the other dimension with me?"
She asked him something like that, he said.{p}What do you think Yoshioka said to that?
Let's go together
I can't go with you
He said nothing

He must have really loved her.
Yoshioka answered without hesitation.
She was overjoyed, he said.
It was the kind of story that made me blush just listening to it.{p}

So the two of them snuck into the school in the middle of the night.
It was kind of like eloping.
Two young lovers, hand in hand, quietly running away without their parents knowing.
The only difference was that they weren't running off to the ends of the earth, but to another dimension.
The two of them weren't scared at all.
Well, of course not.
After all, they were full of hope.{p}

The moment drew closer, second by second.
They'd only get one chance.
If they missed 3:33 and 33 seconds exactly, they couldn't get to the other dimension.
At last, the fateful moment came.
At that instant, they both pressed their hands to the mirror.
...But guess what happened.{p}

Yoshioka's timing was off, just slightly.
Right before his eyes, Meguro faded like mist and was sucked into the mirror.
Yoshioka was left there all alone.
No matter how much he called and screamed, there was no answer.
The mirror showed nothing but his own reflection.
Yoshioka prayed it was all a dream.
But it wasn't.
From the next day on, Meguro was gone.
And ever since then, he said, Yoshioka had been sneaking into the school every night, standing in front of that mirror, and putting his hands on it when the time came.
But maybe his timing was still just a little off, because no matter how many times he tried, it never worked once.
After agonizing over it, he wanted someone to help him, so he came to me for advice.{p}

Can you believe a story like that?
He told me all that with a straight face, totally serious.
I knew Meguro had stopped coming to school.
She was in a different class, but news like that spreads fast.
But I hadn't heard anything about her getting sucked into a mirror.
People were saying whatever they liked: she'd gone missing, she'd run away from home, she was refusing to come to school.
I figured Yoshioka had lost it after his beloved Meguro disappeared.{p}

"Please. I have to see Meguro no matter what.
I bet she's lonely all by herself.
She must be waiting for me to come, looking forward to it the whole time.
Please help me."
He begged me like that, looking like he'd burst into tears any second.
He was being such a pain that I said it lightly, just to get out of the situation.
"Yeah, sure. I'll be waiting in front of the school gate at three."
That's what I said.
He gave me this creepy, happy grin.
Now that I think about it, that was the first time I'd ever seen him smile.
The first and last smile I ever saw on him.{p}

So I went home after school, and for a while I forgot all about it.
It was late at night, and I was thinking about going to bed, when Yoshioka's face suddenly popped into my head.
I looked at the clock: two in the morning.
If I wanted to, I could still make it in time.
Whenever I remembered that creepy grin of his, I just couldn't get to sleep.
But going all the way to school now was such a pain.
Plus, if he didn't show up, I'd be the one who looked like an idiot.
Should I go or shouldn't I? I agonized over it.{p}So what do you think I did in the end?
You went to the school
You didn't go to the school

It just kept nagging at me, you know.
So I decided to go.{p}

No matter how much he liked her, there was no way he could go along with a story like that, right?
Yoshioka told her flat out.
"Don't talk such nonsense.
Open your eyes and live in the real world."
That's what he said.
And then, with tears welling up in her eyes, she vanished from in front of him, just like that.
And that was the last time he ever saw her.
She must have believed Yoshioka would come with her.
And that same Yoshioka betrayed her.
It must have been a huge shock.{p}

The next day, she didn't come to school.
Or the day after, or the day after that.
At first Yoshioka figured she had a cold, or was faking sick a little, but he got more and more worried.
Then weird rumors started going around school.
That Meguro had gone missing, or run away from home, stuff like that.
Yoshioka was the only one who knew about that talk they'd had.
Of course, he didn't actually believe that story about the mirror.
Even so, he felt responsible.
If only he'd taken what she said more seriously back then, it wouldn't have come to this. She'd never have run away from home, he thought.
No matter how long he waited, she didn't come back.
Not a single word from her, either.
Even so, Yoshioka couldn't forget her.
In fact, it was only once she was gone that he realized how much she meant to him.
He wanted to see her.
He wanted to see her so badly he couldn't stand it.
But he had no idea where she was.
And then, one day...{p}

Yoshioka was lying on the bed in his room, spacing out, when all of a sudden, what does he hear but laughter coming out of thin air.
"Ahahahaha... ahahahaha..."
It sounded like someone having the time of their life.
It felt more strange than creepy.
A voice with a sort of echo on it, coming out of empty space.
It got louder, then softer, like someone was fiddling with the volume at random. A strange voice that didn't sound like it belonged to this world.
"Meguro! Meguro, where are you?!"
Yoshioka knew right away whose voice it was.
There was no way he could forget it. It was her voice.
But the voice didn't answer him.
It ignored Yoshioka and just kept on laughing.
That's when Yoshioka remembered something he'd forgotten all this time.
That's right. The story about the mirror.
He'd written it off as a joke from the start, so he'd forgotten all about that mirror.
No, maybe he'd been trying to forget it.
"Ahahaha... It's so fun. Ahahahaha... It's so funny."
The voice sounded truly happy.
And it was as if it had forgotten all about Yoshioka.
"...Meguro. Did you really go to another dimension?
Did you pass through that mirror into the world of another dimension?"
Yoshioka murmured, as if trying to convince himself.{p}

And then, just like that, the voice faded away.
And he never heard it again.
Yoshioka wanted to see Meguro so badly he couldn't bear it.
And he started to think that if he went to that mirror on the landing, he'd be able to see her.{p}

So he went.
He worked up his courage and went and stood in front of that mirror.
But nothing happened.
No matter how many times he went, nothing happened.
Well, of course not.
The guy went there in broad daylight.
He'd have to go at 3:33:33 a.m. after all, Yoshioka thought with a sigh.
But he was scared.
He was scared of going to a place like that alone in the middle of the night.{p}

So he came to me for advice.
But do you think I'd believe a story like that?
The more serious Yoshioka looked as he talked, the funnier I found it.
It was all I could do to keep from laughing.
"Please. All you have to do is come with me.
The school in the middle of the night is scary when you're alone.
Please, I'm begging you, come with me."
I was getting pretty fed up.
He was being such a pest about it that I said it offhand, just to get rid of him.
"Yeah, sure. I'll be waiting in front of the school gate at three."
That's what I said.
He gave me this creepy, happy grin.
Now that I think about it, that might've been the first time I'd ever seen him smile.
The first and last smile I ever saw on him.{p}

So I went home after school, and for a while I forgot all about it.
It was late at night, and I was thinking about going to bed, when Yoshioka's face suddenly popped into my head.
I looked at the clock: two in the morning.
If I wanted to, I could still make it in time.
Whenever I remembered that creepy grin of his, I just couldn't get to sleep.
But going all the way to school now was such a pain.
Plus, if he didn't show up, I'd be the one who looked like an idiot.
Should I go or shouldn't I? I agonized over it.{p}So what do you think I did in the end?
You went to the school
You didn't go to the school

It just kept nagging at me, you know.
So I decided to go.{p}

Right.
You can't answer something like that when it's sprung on you out of nowhere.
"I love her, so I'll go with her."
Anyone who says that is just a spoiled little kid.
Grown-up love is the kind that grows by fighting against adversity.
You'd better remember that, too.
On that point, Yoshioka was a grown-up.
It's just, he was kind of clumsy, I guess...
He was bad with words, couldn't get across even half of what he was thinking.
I'm amazed a guy like that ever got a girlfriend.
Anyway, Yoshioka couldn't give her an answer right away, and he stayed silent for a long time.

For three days after that,
Meguro didn't come to school.
They'd just had a fight, so Yoshioka was worried, of course.
But on the morning of the fourth day, Meguro showed up at school.
She said she'd been off sick with a cold.
Yoshioka apologized to her right away.
And he told her that if she really wanted to go to another dimension, he'd go with her.
Not seeing you for just three days hurt this much,
he said.
He'd realized how much she meant to him.
But Meguro's answer was,
"Ew, what are you talking about? I'm not interested in other dimensions."
Cold as ice.
"You're angry, aren't you? It was all my fault."
"I'm not angry. I don't feel anything for you at all."
At first Yoshioka thought she was just angry, but little by little he started to notice something was off about Meguro.
I couldn't see it at all, though.
According to Yoshioka, she was like a completely different person.
I was listening, only half believing him, when something suddenly came back to me.
Meguro was supposed to be left-handed.
She and I were in the same class in first year, see.
I remember our arms bumping over and over when I sat next to her.
Yoshioka had pointed that out too.
The Meguro of now, it seemed, was right-handed.{p}

That's when I finally got interested in this story too.
Yoshioka's idea was really simple.
The one here now isn't the real Meguro.
See? Simple, right?{p}

Yoshioka remembered that story about the mirror.
Meguro must have gone to the other dimension on her own.
And something else was here in this world, pretending to be Meguro.
To see the real Meguro, he'd have to stand in front of that mirror at 3:33:33 a.m. after all. He kept insisting on it, real passionate.
"Well then, just go."
That's what I told him.
I mean, right?
If he'd figured out that much, it was simple.{p}

Then he let out a sigh and muttered just one thing.
"I'm scared."
That's all.
The old building is scary even in the daytime, and he was terrified of going there alone in the middle of the night.
So that's why he came to me for advice.
"Please. All you have to do is come with me.
The school in the middle of the night is scary when you're alone.
Please, I'm begging you, come with me."
Sure enough, here it came.
And Meguro had managed it on her own, I bet...
Well, it was a little out there, but it sounded like an interesting story.
So I gave him a casual answer.
"Yeah, sure. I'll be waiting in front of the school gate at three."
That's what I said.
He gave me this creepy, happy grin.
Now that I think about it, that might've been the first time I'd ever seen him smile.
That's how bad he was at showing his feelings.{p}

The school at night was creepy.
Knowing Yoshioka, I figured he'd be waiting, but he wasn't there.
I thought he'd gone home, but there was a note stuck on the school gate.
It said he'd gone on ahead.
I'm too nice for my own good, huh?
I went after Yoshioka.
I'd come all the way to the school, so I couldn't rest until I saw it through.{p}

The school at night is freaking scary.
Even the new building is creepy, and I was headed for the old one.
You can imagine how scary that was, right?
Even a haunted house isn't that scary.
I'm amazed a scaredy-cat like Yoshioka made it through there alone.{p}

At night, the sound of your steps on the floorboards is really loud.
Creak, creak, creak, creak. A sound like fingernails scratching glass echoes all around you.
You can't hear anything else, right?
So that sound really grates on your ears.
And the musty smell of old, rotting wood that you hardly notice in the daytime, at night you can smell it clearly.
When you breathe in, that smell is all there is, filling your mouth, thick and stifling.
I couldn't catch up with Yoshioka, but it looked like I'd somehow make it in time.{p}

It was when I got to the spot where you can see that mirror if you go up these stairs.
Someone had gotten there before me.
And let me tell you, it wasn't Yoshioka.
Yoshioka was already in front of the mirror.
This someone was hiding pretty close to Yoshioka, keeping dead still.
Well, I'll get to that someone later.
I hid even farther back, where I could keep watch on the two of them.
I've got good eyesight, and I can see well in the dark.
So it was no problem.{p}

Still, a mirror that connects to another dimension, huh.
Hmm, any way you looked at it, it was just a dingy old mirror.
All it showed was Yoshioka's reflection.
It was almost 3:33:33.
What on earth was supposed to happen?
Just a little longer...
The time was closing in.
Yoshioka pressed his trembling hands to the mirror and waited for the moment.
If Meguro really was in another dimension, he should be able to see her.
3:33:33...
And I was stunned.{p}

Believe it or not, the figure of a woman rose up inside the mirror.
It was Meguro.
"Meguro!"
Yoshioka cried out before he knew it.
And at that instant☆
The forehead of the Meguro in the mirror split wide open, and blood came spraying out.
I was far enough away that I was fine, but Yoshioka took it full in the face.

Meguro disappeared behind a red curtain.
And in her place, Yoshioka's reflection appeared.
You think that's nothing special?
Well, I couldn't believe my eyes.
The Yoshioka in the mirror grabbed both arms of the Yoshioka on this side and pulled.
In the blink of an eye, Yoshioka was inside the mirror.
And standing in front of the mirror was the other Yoshioka.
You get what that means, right?
They switched places.
The two of them, facing each other across the mirror, traded places.
Inside the mirror, Yoshioka looked like he was desperately screaming something.
A way to save him?
The only way would be to switch them back again.
But that's impossible now.
The mirror got smashed.
Remember how I said someone had gotten there before me?{p}

The one there ahead of me was Meguro.
The one who came from the other side of the mirror, that is.{p}

She waited for Yoshioka to switch places, and then she smashed the mirror to pieces.
It was something else.
